paper_title: Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs A Variance Decomposition   Framework
caption: : Meaningful Variability Share
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the distribution of “MVS” and “1-MVS” values across four categories: Health and Nutrition, Logistics, Personal Finance, and Travel and Transportation, for both “70B llama” and “8B llama” models. The horizontal axis represents the categories and model sizes, labeled “70B llama” and “8B llama” in alphabetical order within each category, while the vertical axis represents a value ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each category displays two stacked bars, one for each model size. The lower portion of each bar is colored teal and represents “MVS”, while the upper portion is colored blue and represents “1-MVS”. In Health and Nutrition, the “70B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.4 and a “1-MVS” value of approximately 0.6, while the “8B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.3 and a ”1-MVS” value of approximately 0.7. In Logistics, the “70B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.3 and a “1-MVS” value of approximately 0.7, while the “8B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.2 and a ”1-MVS” value of approximately 0.8. In Personal Finance, the “70B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.4 and a “1-MVS” value of approximately 0.6, while the “8B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.3 and a ”1-MVS” value of approximately 0.7. Finally, in Travel and Transportation, the “70B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.3 and a “1-MVS” value of approximately 0.7, while the “8B llama” model has an “MVS” value of approximately 0.2 and a ”1-MVS” value of approximately 0.8. No bars are visually emphasized.
